#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Keep this project's workflow layer in step with the kit it was made from.

Every project made from the kit carries its own copy of the workflow layer (the
protocols, hooks, scripts and guides).  Without a tool, improvements made in one
project reach the others by hand or not at all.  This script is that tool: the
project pins one kit release in ``local/kit/pin.json``; the kit ships the list of
files it manages in ``local/kit/MANAGED``; git does every merge.

Subcommands (common options: ``--root`` the project, default the repository this
script lives in; ``--offline`` never fetch; ``--to TAG`` the kit release to compare
with, default the newest ``v*`` tag of the kit clone):

  status [--json]            classify every managed path against the pinned release
                             and the target.  Exit 0 nothing pending from the kit,
                             3 kit updates pending, 2 precondition error.
  upgrade [--branch NAME] [--in-place]
                             bring the target release in on branch kit-upgrade-<TAG>:
                             kit-only changes are written, both-sided changes go
                             through ``git merge-file`` (``--union`` for the ledger),
                             the pin is moved, and an EVOLUTION.md entry and an
                             events.md line are appended.  Never commits.  Exit 0
                             clean, 4 conflicts left in the files, 2 precondition.
  contribute [--out PATH]    the project's own changes to managed files as one patch
                             in KIT form, for a kit pull request, written to --out or
                             to <paths.cache_root>/kit/contrib/ (never into the work
                             tree, which ``upgrade`` needs clean).  The project's
                             ledger (EVOLUTION.md) is left out: past the kit's entries
                             it is the project's history.  Exit 5 (patch written with
                             a ``.blocked`` suffix) when a project name survived the
                             reverse rename.
  adopt --repo URL --version TAG
                             first pin of a project that has none, or completion of
                             one bootstrap left without a repository or tag (its
                             local_only, shield and aliases are kept); then ``status``.
                             Credentials in an https URL are dropped from the pin.
  pin [--version TAG] [--local-only PATH REASON]
                             move the pin after a manual sync, or record a deliberate
                             project-only divergence of a managed file.

Reading ``status`` for completion criterion C9 (``local/protocols/completion.md``):
run it with ``--to`` the pinned version; the criterion holds when every
``project-modified``, ``both`` and ``project-only`` path other than
``local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`` is ``local-only`` instead or is named, with its kit
pull request, in the completion comment.  The exit code does not decide C9: it only
says whether the kit has something the project has not taken.

Why the details are as they are:

* The kit is kept in kit form (the placeholder Lean root and slugs of the constants
  below); a project is in project form (its Lean root and slugs, from
  ``local/project.json``).  ``projectform`` is the
  bootstrap rename; ``kitform`` is its inverse, with ``shield`` literals protected
  (links to an ancestor project that merely contain the Lean root) and ``aliases``
  (earlier slugs of the same project) folded in.  Two versions of a file count as
  equal when they agree in kit form OR in project form: kit form tolerates old
  aliases, project form tolerates a kit text that happens to contain the project's
  Lean root as a substring, which the plain inverse rename cannot restore.
* Release trees are materialised with ``read-tree`` + ``checkout-index``, never
  ``git archive``: the kit's ``.gitattributes`` marks the workflow layer
  ``export-ignore`` for project artifacts, and an archive silently drops it.
* ``docs/origin/`` and ``local/kit/`` are never renamed, in either direction, exactly
  as the bootstrap leaves them: the extraction script there carries the placeholders
  the rename is made of.
* ``contribute`` builds the kit-form text line by line against the pinned file: a
  line the project did not change is the kit's line verbatim, so a kit line that
  holds the Lean root as a plain substring is never rewritten by the inverse rename.
  The token check looks at added lines and paths only, and a token must stand
  between non-alphanumeric characters to count (a short name inside an ordinary word
  is not a hit); ``shield`` literals are exempt.
* ``upgrade`` only moves forward: a target that is an ancestor of the pin is refused.
* Nothing is written outside the project root, ``paths.cache_root`` (the kit clone,
  extracted trees, merge scratch files) and ``--out``.
* Files that are not UTF-8 are compared as bytes and never merged.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime
import difflib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Union

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import project_config  # noqa: E402

#: The kit's placeholders, spelled in pieces: the bootstrap rewrites the literal
#: strings across the whole tree, including this file, and the kit-form tokens
#: must survive that rewrite or the instantiated project could not map back.
PLACEHOLDER_ROOT = "Paper" + "Lib"
PLACEHOLDER_OWNER = "OWNER"
PLACEHOLDER_REPO = "REPO"
PLACEHOLDER_SLUG = PLACEHOLDER_OWNER + "/" + PLACEHOLDER_REPO
PLACEHOLDER_COMPARATOR = PLACEHOLDER_SLUG + "-comparator"

MANIFEST = "local/kit/MANAGED"
PIN = "local/kit/pin.json"
EVOLUTION = "local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md"
EVENTS = "results/telemetry/events.md"
#: Append-only on both sides, so a union merge is exact and never conflicts.  Never
#: contributed: past the kit's entries it holds the project's own history (its


@dataclass
class Tokens:
    """The bootstrap rename between kit form and this project's form."""

    lean_root: str
    slug: str
    comparator: str
    aliases: dict[str, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    shields: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg: dict, pin: dict | None = None) -> "Tokens":
        pin = pin or {}
        slug = project_config.get(cfg, "project.github_slug", "") or PLACEHOLDER_SLUG
        return cls(
            lean_root=project_config.get(cfg, "project.lean_root", "") or PLACEHOLDER_ROOT,
            slug=slug,
            comparator=project_config.get(cfg, "project.comparator_slug", "")
            or slug + "-comparator",
            aliases={k: [v for v in vs if v] for k, vs in (pin.get("aliases") or {}).items()},
            shields=[s for s in pin.get("shield") or [] if s])

    def _groups(self) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
        """(placeholder, project value), longest first: the comparator slug contains the slug."""
        return [(PLACEHOLDER_COMPARATOR, self.comparator), (PLACEHOLDER_SLUG, self.slug),
                (PLACEHOLDER_ROOT, self.lean_root)]

    def projectform(self, text: str) -> str:
        for placeholder, value in self._groups():
            if value and value != placeholder:
                text = text.replace(placeholder, value)
        return text

    def kitform(self, text: str) -> str:
        shields = sorted(set(self.shields), key=len, reverse=True)
        salt = 0
        while f"{salt}:" in text:     # a nonce the text cannot already contain
            salt += 1
        nonces = [f"{salt}:{i}" for i in range(len(shields))]
        for shield, nonce in zip(shields, nonces):
            text = text.replace(shield, nonce)
        for placeholder, value in self._groups():
            literals = sorted({value, *self.aliases.get(placeholder, [])}, key=len, reverse=True)
            for literal in literals:
                if literal and literal != placeholder:
                    text = text.replace(literal, placeholder)
        for shield, nonce in zip(shields, nonces):
            text = text.replace(nonce, shield)
        return text

    def same(self, ours: Blob, kit: Blob) -> bool:
        """Project file `ours` equals kit file `kit` in kit form or in project form."""
        if isinstance(ours, bytes) or isinstance(kit, bytes):
            return ours == kit
        return self.kitform(ours) == kit or ours == self.projectform(kit)

    def at(self, path: str) -> "Tokens":
        """The mapping for one kit-form path: the identity under NO_RENAME_PREFIXES."""
        if path.startswith(NO_RENAME_PREFIXES):
            return Tokens(PLACEHOLDER_ROOT, PLACEHOLDER_SLUG, PLACEHOLDER_COMPARATOR)
        return self

    def kit_diff_text(self, base: str, ours: str) -> str:
        """`ours` in kit form, line-aligned with `base`: a line of `ours` that equals the
        project form of a base line becomes that base line, and only the other lines
        go through `kitform`.  The inverse rename alone would also rewrite unchanged
        kit lines that contain the Lean root as a plain substring."""
        base_lines = base.splitlines(keepends=True)
        ours_lines = ours.splitlines(keepends=True)
# ── contribute ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def git_mode(path: Path | None) -> str:
    return "100755" if path is not None and path.stat().st_mode & 0o111 else "100644"


def file_diff(path: str, old: str | None, new: str | None,
              old_mode: str = "100644", new_mode: str = "100644") -> str:
    """A git-apply-compatible diff of one text file (None = absent)."""
    head = [f"diff --git a/{path} b/{path}\n"]
    if old is None:
        head.append(f"new file mode {new_mode}\n")
    elif new is None:
        head.append(f"deleted file mode {old_mode}\n")
    elif old_mode != new_mode:
        head += [f"old mode {old_mode}\n", f"new mode {new_mode}\n"]
    lines = list(difflib.unified_diff(
        (old or "").splitlines(keepends=True), (new or "").splitlines(keepends=True),
        fromfile="/dev/null" if old is None else f"a/{path}",
        tofile="/dev/null" if new is None else f"b/{path}"))
    if not lines:
        return "".join(head) if len(head) == 3 else ""
    body = []
    for line in lines:
        body.append(line if line.endswith("\n") else line + "\n\\ No newline at end of file\n")
    return "".join(head + body)


def project_tokens(cfg: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Names that identify this project and must not reach the kit.  Values still
    equal to the kit's placeholder defaults name no project and are skipped."""
    d = project_config.DEFAULTS
    slug = project_config.get(cfg, "project.github_slug", "") or ""
    owner, _, repo = slug.partition("/")
    candidates = [project_config.get(cfg, "project.lean_root", ""), owner, repo,
                  project_config.get(cfg, "project.comparator_slug", ""),
                  Path(str(project_config.get(cfg, "paths.cache_root", ""))).name,
                  project_config.get(cfg, "session.tmux", ""),
                  *(project_config.get(cfg, "keys", {}) or {})]
    placeholders = {PLACEHOLDER_ROOT, PLACEHOLDER_OWNER, PLACEHOLDER_REPO,
                    PLACEHOLDER_SLUG, PLACEHOLDER_COMPARATOR,
                    Path(d["paths"]["cache_root"]).name, d["session"]["tmux"], *d["keys"]}
    return sorted({str(c) for c in candidates if c and str(c) not in placeholders})


def token_hits(patch: str, tokens: list[str], shields: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Scan what the patch adds (the `+` lines and the paths); context and removed lines
    are the kit's own text.  Token matches need a non-alphanumeric boundary so that a
    short name does not fire inside an ordinary word; shield literals are exempt."""
    if not tokens:
        return []
    regex = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])(%s)(?![A-Za-z0-9])"
                       % "|".join(re.escape(t) for t in sorted(tokens, key=len, reverse=True)))
    hits = []
    for number, line in enumerate(patch.splitlines(), 1):
        if not (line.startswith("+") or line.startswith("diff --git ")):
            continue
        for shield in shields:
            line = line.replace(shield, "")
        for match in regex.finditer(line):
            hits.append(f"patch line {number}: project token {match.group(1)!r}")
    return hits


def cmd_contribute(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    root, cfg, pin, clone, target = context(args)
    p = plan(root, cfg, pin, clone, target)
    tokens = Tokens.from_config(cfg, pin)
    base_dir = extract(clone, p.base_sha, cfg)
    chunks, skipped = [], []
    for e in p.entries:
        if e.cls not in ("project-modified", "both", "project-only"):
            continue
        if e.path in UNION_MERGED:
            print(f"left out: {e.ppath} is the project's own ledger; add the ledger entry of a "
                  f"generic amendment to the kit's copy by hand in the kit PR", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        if e.binary:
            skipped.append(e.ppath)
            continue
        mapping = tokens.at(e.path)
        new = None if e.ours is None else (
            mapping.kitform(e.ours) if e.base is None else mapping.kit_diff_text(e.base, e.ours))
        chunks.append(file_diff(
            e.path, e.base, new,
            old_mode=git_mode(base_dir / e.path if e.base is not None else None),
            new_mode=git_mode(root / e.ppath if e.ours is not None else None)))
    for path in skipped:
        print(f"skipped (not UTF-8, contribute by hand): {path}", file=sys.stderr)
    patch = "".join(chunks)
    if not patch:
        print(f"nothing to contribute against kit {p.pinned}")
        return EXIT_OK
    # the default lies outside the work tree: an untracked patch there would make the
    # tree dirty, and `upgrade` (the next step of the kit-first sequence) refuses that
    out = Path(args.out).expanduser().resolve() if args.out else \
        cache_root(cfg) / "kit" / "contrib" / f"kit-contrib-{today()}.patch"
    hits = token_hits(patch, project_tokens(cfg), tokens.shields)
    if hits:
        out = out.with_name(out.name + ".blocked")
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(patch, encoding="utf-8")
    if hits:
        for hit in hits:
            print(f"kit_sync.py: {hit}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"kit_sync.py: blocked; edit {out} (kit form only) and drop the .blocked suffix",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_BLOCKED
    lean = (project_config.get(cfg, "project.lean_root", "") or "project").lower()
    branch = f"contrib/{lean}-{today()}"
    print(f"wrote {out} (kit form, against {p.pinned})")
    print("open the kit pull request with:")
    print(f"  git -C {clone} checkout -b {branch} {p.pinned}")
    print(f"  git -C {clone} apply --index {out} && git -C {clone} commit -m "
          f"\"Contribute from {lean}\"")
    print(f"  cd {clone} && git push -u origin {branch} && gh pr create --fill")
    return EXIT_OK


# ── adopt, pin ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def cmd_adopt(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
def cmd_adopt(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Write the first pin, or complete one that bootstrap left without a repository or
    a release tag; `local_only`, `shield` and `aliases` of such a pin are kept."""
    root = Path(args.root).expanduser().resolve()
    cfg = load_config(root)
    kept: dict = {}
    if (root / PIN).exists():
        old = read_pin(root, complete=False)
        if not incomplete(old) and old.get("commit"):
            raise Refused(f"{PIN} exists; use `kit_sync.py pin --version TAG` to move it")
        kept = {k: old[k] for k in ("shield", "aliases", "local_only") if k in old}
    repo = args.repo
    if Path(repo).expanduser().is_dir():
        repo = str(Path(repo).expanduser().resolve())
    clone = ensure_clone(cfg, repo, args.offline)     # the clone may use the credentials
    sha = resolve(clone, args.version)
    write_pin(root, {"schema": 1, "repo": scrub_url(repo), "version": args.version,
                     "commit": sha, "adopted": today(), "upgraded": today(), **kept})
    print(f"pinned kit {args.version} ({sha[:12]}) in {PIN}")
    target = args.to or newest_tag(clone)
    return report_status(root, plan(root, cfg, read_pin(root), clone, target), False)


def cmd_pin(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    root = Path(args.root).expanduser().resolve()
    cfg = load_config(root)
    pin = read_pin(root, complete=False)      # bootstrap may have left `version` empty
    if not args.version and not args.local_only:
        raise Refused("pin needs --version TAG or --local-only PATH REASON")
    if args.version:
        if "repo" in incomplete(pin):
            raise Refused(f"{PIN} names no kit repository; run `kit_sync.py adopt --repo URL "
                          f"--version TAG` (it completes the pin and keeps the rest)")
        clone = ensure_clone(cfg, pin["repo"], args.offline)
        pin.update(version=args.version, commit=resolve(clone, args.version))
    if args.local_only:
        path, reason = args.local_only[0].strip(), args.local_only[1].strip()
        if not path or not reason:
            raise Refused("--local-only needs a path and a non-empty one-line reason")
        pin.setdefault("local_only", {})[path] = " ".join(reason.split())
    write_pin(root, pin)
    version, commit = pin.get("version") or "(no version)", pin.get("commit") or ""
    print(f"updated {PIN}: kit {version} ({commit[:12]})")
    return EXIT_OK

## What runs where

| Layer | Where it lives | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| meta session | your terminal | supervises; talks to you; never proves |
| main session | a `tmux` pane on the work machine | the operator: briefs, dispatches, gates, records |
| workers | detached processes, own worktrees | the mathematics |
| session layer | `local/bin/session/` | launch, message, goal keeper, key watch, pause, stand-down, status |
| service layer | `local/bin/service/` | merge daemon, lanes, review gate, trains, records — all model-free |
| project workflow | `local/bin/`, `scripts/`, `.githooks/` | issues, pull requests, CI, review, audits, completion gate |
| project identity | `local/project.json` | names, paths, issues, caps, keys — read by everything |
| runtime state | `$KIT_STATE_DIR` (outside the repository) | goal text, markers, claims, logs, the running handoff file |

CI, reviews and merges **execute locally**; GitHub holds the record. The
`.github/` tree is kept as frozen reference for the mechanisms the local
scripts replace, and is not executed here.

## How the rules evolve

The protocols under `local/protocols/` are normative until amended. An agent
that finds one wrong does not deviate: it records the friction in
`results/telemetry/events.md`, and an amendment is made with a cited trigger
and an entry in `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`. No trigger, no amendment. That
is `local/protocols/meta.md`, and it is what makes the kit improve instead of
drifting.

## One kit, many projects

Every project built from this kit carries a copy of the workflow layer. The
files the kit owns are listed in `local/kit/MANAGED` (gitignore-style
patterns); everything else — the Lean library, the paper, `local/project.json`,
`results/` (except the owner tools under `results/telemetry/owner-tools/` and
`results/telemetry/model-comparison/compare.py`), `local/briefs/` and
`local/registry/` (except their READMEs), this README — belongs to the
project. `local/kit/pin.json` records which kit release the copy is
(repository, tag, commit), plus any managed file the project deliberately keeps
different, each with a one-line reason (`local_only`).

`scripts/kit_sync.py` keeps the copy honest, with git as the merge engine:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `status [--to TAG]` | classifies every managed file against the pinned kit and the target release: unchanged, modified here, recorded `local_only`, updated in the kit, changed on both sides, new or removed in the kit |
| `upgrade --to TAG` | brings a release in as ONE branch and pull request through the project's normal gate: three-way merges, conflicts left marked and listed, the pin updated, an `EVOLUTION.md` entry and an `events.md` line written; it never commits |
| `contribute` | writes the project's changes to managed files as a patch in kit form (project names mapped back to the placeholders; the patch goes under `paths.cache_root`, and the project's own `EVOLUTION.md` entries stay out of it), refuses if a project name survives, and prints the commands that open the kit pull request |
| `adopt --repo URL --version TAG` | first pin for a project that was instantiated without one, or completes a pin the bootstrap could only partly write |
| `pin --version TAG`, `pin --local-only PATH "reason"` | records a manual sync, or a deliberate divergence |

The rule that goes with it is **kit first** (`local/protocols/meta.md`,
Amendment procedure step 6): a generic amendment — not about this paper, this
machine or this run — is made where the incident happened and contributed to
the kit in the same episode; a project-only divergence is recorded as
`local_only`. Completion criterion **C9** (`local/protocols/completion.md`)
enforces it: a track is not finished while the pin is missing or malformed, or
while a managed file diverges from the pinned kit without being contributed or
recorded. The gate checks the pin; the `kit_sync.py status --to <pinned
version>` run attached to the completion comment covers the rest (every file it
lists as changed here, the ledger aside, is `local_only` or named with its kit
pull request).

## Honest status

- The workflow this kit is made of was **proven on exactly one project**: a
  Lean formalization of a research paper, taken from an empty repository to
  zero `sorry` with an independent comparator check, over about three weeks,
  by a supervised autonomous session with detached workers.
- The **bootstrap path itself is new**, and it was deliberately tested lightly.
  What was exercised: the unit tests under `scripts/tests/` (about 1,400, all
  offline); the live fetch and the byte-exact split on one real arXiv e-print
  (a 200-page paper, 16 section files); and, on a scratch copy, the whole
  instantiation path — rename, fresh git history, first commit with the hooks
# Meta-protocol — how this workflow evolves

Read this before any other protocol. It governs how the protocols themselves
change, and the telemetry duties that make the project usable as research data.

## Standing principles

1. **Protocols are normative until amended.** An agent that finds a protocol
   wrong, ambiguous, or costly does not silently deviate: it follows the
   protocol (or stops), records the friction in
   `results/telemetry/events.md`, and proposes an amendment — a dispatched
   worker proposes it to the operator; the operator amends directly under the
   procedure below, an `events.md` incident being a sufficient trigger.  Owner
   action is needed only for actual access/permission blockers under
   `issues-prs.md` §6 (2026-09-06T05:05Z); main owns mathematical/internal
   workflow decisions, including previously posted B7/B8. This does not waive
   proof integrity, normal gates or the requirement to record bounded authority.
2. **Amendments are evidence-driven.** Every change to a file under
   `local/protocols/` or to `AGENTS.md` must append an entry to
   `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` citing its trigger: an `events.md` incident,
   a telemetry observation (e.g. repeated duplicate builds in
   `builds.jsonl`), or an upstream policy decision by the user. No trigger,
   no amendment.
3. **The parent repo is precedent, not law.** The GitHub-era mechanism (frozen
   under `.github/`, mapped in `local/DESIGN.md`) is the default answer to
   "how should this work?"; deviations are fine when the local setting
   genuinely differs, and must be recorded in `EVOLUTION.md` with the reason.
   Generic mechanism now lives in the kit repository that `local/kit/pin.json`
   names, not in the parent repo alone: this project holds a pinned copy of it
   (`local/kit/MANAGED` lists the files), and step 6 below says which way a
   change to that copy travels.
4. **De-automation is a valid evolution step.** The parent workflow repeatedly
   demoted LLM agents to deterministic scripts once the mechanical half of a
   job was understood (issue-automation.yml:13-21), and demoted CI jobs to
   notices when resources were exhausted. Prefer the cheapest mechanism that
   holds the invariant.
5. **Two memory disciplines.** Reports and session records are append-only and
   never rewritten (supersede with dated status notes). Protocol documents
   and paper-gap notes are living documents that are rewritten in place
   (history lives in git and `EVOLUTION.md`). Do not mix the two.

## Amendment procedure

1. Write the incident/observation in `results/telemetry/events.md` (dated).
2. Draft the protocol edit.
3. Append to `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`:
   `## YYYY-MM-DD — <short title>` with fields **Trigger** (cite events.md
   entry or telemetry line), **Change** (files + gist), **Expected effect**,
   and, when known later, **Outcome**.
4. Commit protocol edit and ledger entry together, `docs(local)` scope.
5. If the change alters guard semantics (locks, caps, gates, kill switches),
   grep `local/` for every enforcement point and update all of them in the
   same commit — the parent repo maintained such consistency invariants
   through cross-referencing comments; we inherit the same drift risk.
6. **Kit first.** If the change is generic — not about this paper, this
   machine or this run — and touches a file `local/kit/MANAGED` lists, make it
   here where the incident happened, then contribute it to the kit in the same
   episode: `python3 scripts/kit_sync.py contribute` writes the patch in kit
   form and prints the commands that open the kit pull request, which the meta
   session runs (mains never push to the kit repository; `meta-session.md`
   §15). A deliberate
   project-only divergence of a managed file is recorded instead, with its
   reason, by `python3 scripts/kit_sync.py pin --local-only <path> "<reason>"`.
   Kit releases come in through `python3 scripts/kit_sync.py upgrade --to <tag>
   --in-place --root <fresh worktree>` (never in the primary checkout,
   `main-cycle.md` rules 5 and 6) as ONE pull request through the project's
   normal gate; `contribute` writes under `paths.cache_root` unless `--out`
   says otherwise, never into the checkout; the `EVOLUTION.md`
   entry the tool writes is the recorded decision a kit-upgrade commit may cite
   for `MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE=1` when its merged diff exceeds the
   workflow-layer budget. Completion criterion C9 (`completion.md`) holds a
   track open while a managed file diverges without either record.

## Telemetry duties

Schemas (all JSONL, one object per line; timestamps ISO-8601 with offset):

- `results/telemetry/stages.jsonl` —
  `{ts, stage, event: start|end|milestone, note?, tokens_note?}`
  Stages: `1-skeleton`, `2-references`, `3-blueprint`, `4.1-minimal`,
  `4.2-full-skeleton`, `4.3-proofs` (extend as needed).
- `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` —
  `{name, role, model?, account?, requested_effort?, issue, pr?, thread_id,
    start, end, wall_s, usage: {input, cached_input, cache_write, output, reasoning},
    exit, dispatcher, worktree, status: active|done|failed|archived}`
  Written only by `local/bin/dispatch.sh` / `telemetry.py`. New dispatches always
  supply `account` (`primary` or `second`) and the exact resolved `model`
  passed to the CLI (environment override, otherwise selected-account config).
  External rows use allocator accounts `primary|second`; native rows use the
  active key NAME from `keys` in `local/project.json` in both `account` and

    name = re.split(r"[/:\\]", repo.rstrip("/"))[-1]

    if not name:

def ensure_clone(cfg: dict, repo: str, offline: bool) -> Path:
    """Clone on first use, fetch tags otherwise; `--offline` uses what is cached."""
    clone = clone_dir(cfg, repo)
    if (clone / ".git").exists():
        if not offline:
            git(clone, "fetch", "--quiet", "--tags", "--prune", "origin", timeout=120)

    if clone.exists():

    clone.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if rc != 0:
